name: manual_a5b40e
claim: Perpetua-Tools contains TS/JS packages (packages/alphaclaw-adapter/, packages/alphaclaw-mcp/) whose stated purpose is to steer/commandeer AlphaClaw -- but this is a runtime-only relationship, never a repo-level one, and matters for scope decisions under a standing "never touch AlphaClaw's repo" constraint. Verified directly: these packages spawn a local AlphaClaw process (child_process.spawn("node", ["bin/alphaclaw.js", "start"])) and communicate with it over plain HTTP (http.request) once it's running. There is no git clone, checkout, commit, or any other git operation against diazMelgarejo/AlphaClaw anywhere in this code -- it assumes AlphaClaw is already installed/checked out as a sibling and only ever controls the running process and its HTTP surface. Code sharing AlphaClaw's name, or referencing its branches (e.g. a comment naming feature/MacOS-post-install) by way of explaining what it talks to, is not the same as touching AlphaClaw's repository -- this PT-owned code is in scope for PT-side work even when the broader task explicitly excludes AlphaClaw itself.

decisions.notes: Explicit user instruction to record and confirm this runtime-vs-repo-level distinction before proceeding with NPM-packaging work on the controller.

rationale: Explicit user instruction to record and confirm this runtime-vs-repo-level distinction before proceeding with NPM-packaging work on the controller.
